headline: Malicious JavaScript Used To Target Cryptocurrency On Major Sites
metaDescription: Hackers utilized malicious JavaScript on 178 websites to target iPhone users and steal cryptocurrency, impacting various international organizations.
aiSummaryBullets: Malicious JavaScript was discovered on 178 different websites.
The attack targeted iPhone users to facilitate the theft of cryptocurrency.
Affected organizations include entities such as Zoom, HSBC, and Salesforce.
aiContextParagraph: A security compromise involving malicious JavaScript has been identified, affecting visitors to the online platforms of 178 organizations. The scope of the incident includes major global entities such as Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and Ikea. According to reports, the malicious code was specifically designed to target iPhone users with the intent of facilitating cryptocurrency theft. By embedding unauthorized scripts into these reputable websites, attackers sought to exploit unsuspecting visitors. While the full technical details of the breach are being analyzed, this event highlights ongoing concerns regarding web-based security vulnerabilities and the methods used to compromise large-scale digital infrastructure. The incident underscores the risks associated with third-party code integration on high-traffic websites, as attackers continue to find ways to leverage established digital platforms to reach end-users and compromise their financial assets or personal security.
whyItIsViral: This story is generating interest due to the high profile of the compromised organizations and strong public search curiosity regarding the technical nature of the JavaScript exploit.

sources.articleTitle: Popular websites compromised in bid to steal crypto, target iPhone users
